questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.learningObjective: choose an abstract class for shared state plus a partial implementation
questions.stem: A lighthouse network needs one shared foghorn routine plus a stored station name used by every station, while unrelated harbor devices only need a common signal contract. Which design fits?

options.text: An abstract Station class holding the name and foghorn code, plus a Signaler interface for all devices.
An interface holding the station name as instance state for every station.
A single concrete class that every device extends, including unrelated ones.
No shared type at all, with the foghorn routine copied into each class.

questions.explanation: Abstract classes can store shared fields and supply concrete methods, while an interface expresses a contract that unrelated classes can all honor.
questions.hint: Ask which construct can hold a stored name.

questions.learningObjective: state that unrelated classes share interfaces while one lineage shares an abstract class
questions.stem: A bakery program models baguettes, croissants, and delivery vans that can all be discounted, but only the breads share dough state and proofing steps. Which statement about reuse is accurate?

options.text: Breads can extend one shared abstract BakedGood while any class, including the van, implements Discountable.
The van should extend BakedGood so it can be discounted.
options.misconception: unrelated types should share a lineage

options.text: A class can extend several abstract classes at once to collect every behavior.
Interfaces cannot be implemented by classes that already extend something.

questions.explanation: Single inheritance carries the bread lineage once, and interfaces add the discount role to any class regardless of lineage.
questions.hint: Separate the family trait from the extra role.

questions.stem: A trail guide posts four claims about shared types at the ranger station. Which claims are true? Select all that apply.
